name: Harumaph
overview: Harumaph is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Jedaiah, as recorded in Nehemiah 3:10. There is no additional information regarding his tribe or other personal details. His mention is brief and focused on his paternal relationship.
namesAndTitles: The name Harumaph means "disfigured nose" in Hebrew. This proper name is not indicated as being given by God, and it appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Nehemiah 3:10.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Harumaph as the father of Jedaiah, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections or descendants are mentioned.
scriptureSignificance: Harumaph's significance lies in his identification as the father of Jedaiah, who is noted among those involved in the rebuilding efforts described in Nehemiah 3:10. Though Harumaph himself does not have a direct role in the narrative, his mention helps establish the lineage and community context of those contributing to the restoration of Jerusalem.
